Also, when the reader is an agent standing in for a person, the lens has no way to name them","source":"art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, item I8, 2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED (designer, friction-log entry #12): "loop_status's lens said '1 recorded here … none describes themselves' while who:claude and who:owner both carry descriptions." Design: flo2 50f966697d6c5024, 0.74.0.

② PRECEDENT: cap:the-skill-response-carries-the-lens; epoch:the-lens-reaches-the-loop-rail; req:the-agent-says-which-recorded-reader-it-assumes-and-the-lens-names-them.

③ CANDIDATES:
(a) The lens miscounts.
(b) The lens counts only people, and both describing contributors are agents.
(c) A stale cache.
(d) The observation is wrong.

④⑤ MEASURED:
- reflow2-core claims.rs, ReaderLens::from: "An `automated_agent` is deliberately excluded". with_background and without_background hold PEOPLE (kind person or unset) only.
- The design holds who:acct-23984879ca (kind person, no description, minted by flo2) and who:claude and who:owner (both automated_agent, both described).
- get_skill "jot" through flo2 with design 50f966697d6c5024 returned "1 recorded here and none describes themselves (who:acct-23984879ca (Anthony Sligar))", exactly (b).
(a) and (c) are refuted, and (d) is partly true: the count was right and the reading was wrong.

⑥ CLASS. skills.rs lens_line prints "{n} recorded here and none describes themselves" with no noun. So a reader holding the contributor list sees a miscount. A second, real gap sits beside it: in a delegated or two-agent run, the READER may be an agent acting for a person, and the lens's only notion of a reader is a person.

⑦⑧ OWED:
- The wording: "1 PERSON recorded here …, and 2 agents not counted".
- A test pinning that the lens names the excluded agents' count.
Whether a lens should say anything about an agent acting for a principal belongs with the agent-and-principal question, not this finding.
